title: Walmart is beating Amazon in a business worth $35B
summary: Walmart and other traditional retailers are significantly outperforming Amazon in the rapidly growing click-and-collect business, which is estimated to reach $35 billion in sales in the U.S. by 2020. Walmart's grocery pickup program is a major contributor to its U.S. comparable sales growth, while Amazon's efforts in this hybrid online and physical shopping model are described as tentative and lacking a cohesive strategy. The article suggests that Amazon's delayed entry into robust click-and-collect services could lead to lost customer loyalty to competitors and warns that pickup service may be a lasting consumer preference, especially in suburbs.

title: Walgreens Trims Its Fiscal Year Forecast After a Challenging Quarter
summary: Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc. reduced its earnings outlook for the fiscal year after a difficult second quarter, missing Wall Street estimates for both earnings per share and revenue. The company cited pressure from insurers, a weak cold and flu season, and declining tobacco sales for the profit drop. CEO Stefano Pessina vowed a quick response to address these challenges and return to growth, while also acknowledging increased competition from Amazon.

title: Walgreens sees Kroger partnership as a way forward
summary: Walgreens plans to lean on its partnership with Kroger and private label health and beauty offerings to strengthen its business following disappointing Q2 results. The company aims to accelerate digitalization, transform retail offerings, modernize pharmacy, and implement a cost management program. While the Kroger partnership currently involves a small fraction of Walgreens locations, an expanded collaboration could boost grocery capabilities and revenue for both companies.

title: CVS spreads same-day prescription deliveries to 36 states
summary: CVS Health is expanding its same-day prescription delivery service nationwide, covering 36 states and Washington D.C., from 6,000 locations. This move is part of drugstores' efforts to compete with online retailers like Amazon and cater to customers who prefer online shopping and home delivery. The service, costing about $8, also allows for the delivery of other health and baby products, with orders placed through the company's app, text, or phone call, and delivered by Shipt.

title: WWD: Retailer of the Year
summary: American Eagle Outfitters Inc. Executive Chairman and CEO Jay Schottenstein discusses the company's success in navigating the evolving retail landscape, emphasizing its ability to thrive in both brick-and-mortar and e-commerce eras. The article highlights American Eagle's 16 consecutive quarters of comparable sales gains, particularly Aerie's double-digit increases, and its recognition as the American Apparel and Footwear Association’s Retailer of the Year. Schottenstein attributes this success to technological investment, deep customer understanding through analytics, and Aerie's authentic approach to body positivity.

title: CVS to offer same-day prescription delivery via Target-owned Shipt
summary: CVS Health is expanding its same-day prescription delivery service nationwide through a partnership with Target-owned Shipt. This marks Shipt's first entry into the pharmacy space, while CVS is broadening its delivery options beyond its existing one or two-day service. Customers can get same-day delivery for $7.99, or subscribe to Shipt for $99 annually for broader delivery services.

title: Qualcomm Announces New AI Chip for Cloud Data Center Servers
summary: Qualcomm Inc., a leader in smartphone technology, is entering the crowded market for AI chips used in cloud data centers. The company plans to leverage its mobile expertise and advanced manufacturing to deliver power-efficient products, aiming for a share of a market projected to reach $17 billion by 2025. This move positions Qualcomm to compete with established players like Intel, Nvidia, and cloud providers already developing AI components.

title: SoFi Select 500 ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the SoFi Select 500 ETF (SFY), which was created on April 11, 2019, by SoFi. The ETF primarily invests in large-cap US equities selected by market capitalization, currently holding $653.65 million in assets under management across 501 holdings. Key holdings include major technology companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, Amazon, and Apple, alongside recent changes in share counts for various stocks.

title: Stanley Black & Decker CEO: 'Things are going great with Craftsman'
summary: Stanley Black & Decker CEO James Loree claims that the Craftsman brand, acquired from Sears, is performing exceptionally well despite Sears' continued sale of its own Craftsman tools. Loree highlights improvements in product quality and expanded distribution through retailers like Lowe's and Amazon, anticipating significant revenue growth. The company is also in a legal dispute with Sears over the marketing and sale of competing Craftsman products.

title: Twice as many companies paying zero taxes under Trump tax plan
summary: A new analysis by the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy (ITEP) reveals that 60 large U.S. companies paid no federal income taxes in 2018, more than double the average in previous years, despite earning billions in profits. This increase is largely attributed to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, which significantly lowered the corporate tax rate and introduced new tax breaks. Companies like Amazon, Netflix, Chevron, Eli Lilly, and Deere & Co. are among those that effectively paid zero taxes, leading to a substantial impact on the federal budget.

title: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos jabs eBay in shareholder letter over third-party sales
summary: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos criticized eBay in his annual shareholder letter, claiming Amazon's third-party sales growth has significantly outpaced eBay's due to superior seller tools. This led to a stock dip for eBay and a retort from its CEO, Devin Wenig, who highlighted eBay's focus on customers and lack of competition with its sellers. Bezos also challenged other retailers to match Amazon's $15 minimum wage, drawing a response from Walmart.

title: 2018 Letter to Shareholders
summary: Jeff Bezos's 2018 Letter to Shareholders details Amazon's remarkable growth, particularly highlighting the success of third-party sellers on the platform, which now account for 58% of physical gross merchandise sales. Bezos emphasizes Amazon's culture of invention, wandering, and customer obsession, citing examples like AWS, Amazon Go, and Alexa. The letter also addresses Amazon's focus on employee investment, including raising the minimum wage to $15 an hour and supporting education and veterans, while challenging other retailers to match their benefits.

title: Jumia Surges on U.S. Debut as Africa's Amazon Goes Public
summary: Jumia Technologies AG shares soared 75% on their first day of trading in New York, with investors eager to back the company's expansion of online shopping services across Africa. The stock traded at $25.46, valuing the company at over $1.9 billion, after Jumia raised $196 million through the sale of 13.5 million American depositary receipts. This successful debut signifies strong investor interest in "Africa's Amazon."

title: Publicis Buys Alliance Data’s Epsilon for $4.4 Billion in Cash
summary: Publicis Groupe SA is set to acquire Alliance Data Systems Corp.'s digital marketing firm Epsilon for $4.4 billion in cash, marking its largest takeover to date. This move aims to bolster Publicis's presence in the digital marketing sector amid a competitive landscape against tech giants and consulting firms. The acquisition is intended to be fully debt-financed, leading Publicis to suspend its share buyback program.

title: Ulta Beauty’s Canadian expansion plan adds more competition to crowded sector
summary: Ulta Beauty Inc. is planning to expand into Canada as early as late 2020 or early 2021, posing a significant challenge to existing beauty retailers like Hudson's Bay, Shoppers Drug Mart, and Sephora. The U.S. cosmetics giant aims to capitalize on Canada's lucrative beauty market through its distinctive model, which includes in-store salons and a wide range of products from both mass-market and prestige brands. This expansion could also benefit Canadian retail landlords by filling vacant spaces left by struggling merchants.

title: Del Monte Foods makes SAP ERP migration to AWS
summary: Del Monte Foods migrated its SAP ERP system to Amazon Web Services (AWS) to consolidate IT systems, reduce costs, and gain flexibility. This move, driven by prior acquisition challenges, allowed them to cut IT costs by about 35% without disrupting business processes. Analysts noted Del Monte is ahead of the curve in fully moving core ERP to the cloud, as many companies remain on-premises or in vendor-hosted environments.

title: Reliability at heart of Lyft and Uber’s tech, IPOs reveal
summary: This article examines the critical role of reliable technology for rideshare giants Lyft and Uber, as revealed in their IPO filings. It compares their cloud strategies, infrastructure, workforce, and cybersecurity approaches, highlighting how technological reliability underpins their operations and growth in competitive markets. Both companies emphasize data-driven insights and scalable platforms, while also navigating significant challenges like security breaches and regulatory complexities.

title: Best Buy CEO Hubert Joly is stepping down
summary: Hubert Joly, credited with turning around Best Buy Co. Inc., is stepping down as CEO this summer. Chief Financial Officer Corie Barry will succeed him in June. Joly's strategy included utilizing Best Buy's physical space by creating mini-showrooms for other companies, which helped the retailer compete with Amazon.

title: Cloud Computing: The Digital Infrastructure Powering Today's Businesses
summary: This article discusses how cloud computing has fundamentally transformed business IT, moving from on-premise infrastructure to remote, scalable services. It highlights the financial advantages, ease of management, flexibility, platform power, interoperability, and enablement of emerging technologies as key drivers of its growth. The article concludes that while cloud adoption is still relatively early, it is becoming a foundational tool for businesses of all sizes, with increasing spending and widespread implementation expected.

title: Logitech Harmony Express Brings Effortless Voice Control and Easy Navigation to Your Home Entertainment
summary: Logitech announced Harmony Express, a new universal voice remote with built-in Amazon Alexa, designed to simplify home entertainment control. Users can control TV, streaming apps, and smart home devices using voice commands. The remote also features a "remote finder" function through its mobile app or existing Alexa devices.

title: Why O'Reilly Automotive Stock Smashed the Market in 2018
summary: O'Reilly Automotive (ORLY) stock rose significantly in 2018, outperforming the market due to solid same-store-sales growth, a defensive market shift toward recession-resistant stocks, and an aging vehicle fleet. The article highlights that the auto-parts sector's strong performance also eased fears about competition from Amazon.com. Investors are now watching to see if these companies can meet expectations in 2019 after strong 2018 valuations.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper partners to deliver an Adrenaline Shoc to the energy drink category
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper has partnered with beverage entrepreneur Lance Collins to launch Adrenaline Shoc, a new energy drink targeted at the after-workout crowd. This sugar-free beverage, containing 300 mg of caffeine and natural energy boosters, aims to compete in the increasingly crowded energy drink market. Despite a slowdown in the category's growth rate, Keurig Dr Pepper hopes to differentiate Adrenaline Shoc with its "better-for-you" ingredients and premium pricing.

title: Netflix is opening a production hub in NYC
summary: Netflix is expanding its presence in New York City by opening a new production hub, which is expected to create hundreds of jobs and involve up to $100 million in investments. This move follows Amazon backing out of Long Island City and comes as Netflix faces increased competition from other streaming services like Disney, demonstrating its strategy to grow beyond Hollywood. The state of New York is offering Netflix up to $4 million in performance-based tax incentives for job creation.

title: Snap has three years to make a profit before it runs out of money
summary: Snap, once valued at $24 billion upon its 2017 IPO, has just over three years to become profitable before it runs out of cash, according to a Financial Times analysis. Despite a struggling stock price, executive exodus, and a disastrous app redesign, the company is attempting a turnaround by cutting costs and boosting user numbers. Snap faces intense competition from Facebook and needs to broaden its appeal beyond its young demographic to older users and expand its advertising base.

title: Amazon plans to shut down China marketplace in rare retreat
summary: Amazon plans to shut down its Chinese marketplace business in July, shifting its focus to offering mainland consumers overseas products rather than goods from local sellers. This retreat highlights the challenges American tech companies face in competing with strong local leaders like Alibaba and JD.com in China's retail market. While Amazon will maintain other business operations in China, this move signifies a strategic shift to focus on markets like India where it sees a better chance of becoming a dominant player.

title: Kohl's greatly expands partnership with Amazon and offers stock to digital giant
summary: Kohl's is significantly expanding its partnership with Amazon by accepting returns from Amazon customers at all 1,150+ Kohl's stores nationwide, causing Kohl's stock to jump nearly 12%. The department store chain has also granted Amazon the right to buy 1.7 million Kohl's shares, about 1% of outstanding shares. This move follows a successful pilot program in Chicago where Kohl's stores accepting Amazon returns saw an 8% revenue gain compared to 2% elsewhere.

title: Robots in the Permian? Climate concerns drive innovation
summary: Oil supermajors like Chevron and Exxon Mobil are heavily investing in the Permian Basin, using advanced automation, cloud computing, and AI to maximize oil extraction. This strategy is seen as a hedge against future climate change regulations and potential drops in oil demand, allowing for quick returns and flexibility. However, environmentalists criticize the focus on fossil fuels, and some experts question the feasibility of the desired automation and the long-term sustainability of shale production.

title: Ford to Invest $500 Million in Rivian, a Tesla Rival (Published 2019)
summary: Ford Motor has agreed to invest $500 million in Rivian, an electric-car start-up seen as a potential rival to Tesla. This partnership aims to accelerate Ford's electric vehicle development and streamline its operations, while Rivian prepares to launch its own electric pickup truck and SUV. The investment highlights the changing dynamics in the auto industry with newcomers gaining ground through technological advancements.

title: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) earnings Q3 2019
summary: Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT) exceeded revenue and earnings estimates for Q3 2019, causing its shares to rise by 3% in aftermarket hours. The company reported strong growth across its segments, including Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing, driven by demand for cloud offerings and increased engagement in LinkedIn and Xbox Live. Microsoft's CFO highlighted that commercial cloud revenue reached $9.6 billion, marking a 41% year-over-year increase.

title: Variety, iHeartMedia Launch New Film Podcast ‘The Big Ticket’ With Marc Malkin
summary: Variety and iHeartMedia have launched a new weekly film-focused podcast called "The Big Ticket," hosted by Marc Malkin. The podcast will feature interviews with Hollywood stars and filmmakers, with its debut episodes focusing on "Avengers: Endgame" and upcoming guests including Halle Berry and Keanu Reeves. This partnership aims to expand the reach of Variety's journalism to wider audiences through iHeartMedia's platforms.

title: Deal of the Year: Amazon HQ2
summary: The article discusses the significant effort and collaboration involved in securing Amazon's HQ2 for Greater Washington. It highlights the Amazon deal as one of the largest ever for the region and includes related news about Amazon's real estate activities and development efforts by JBG Smith and Brookfield.

title: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) earnings Q1 2019
summary: Amazon.com Inc. surpassed Q1 2019 earnings estimates, with revenues aligning with expectations. Net sales increased 17% year-over-year to $59.7 billion, and net income rose significantly to $3.6 billion. The company provided Q2 2019 sales and operating income guidance and announced expanded YouTube and Prime Video app availability on various devices.

title: Five fund buyers reveal their favourite tech ETFs
summary: This article compiles the favorite tech ETFs of five different fund buyers, highlighting various approaches to gaining tech exposure, including robotics and automation, pure-play sector exposure, and broad Nasdaq 100 coverage that includes FAANG stocks. Each fund buyer explains their rationale for choosing particular ETFs, considering factors like methodology, diversification, liquidity, and how well the ETF captures the evolving definition of "tech."

title: Off-White is Claiming Legal Rights in Quotation Marks and Red Zip Ties, and Suing Over Them
summary: Off-White is asserting exclusive common law trademark rights in its use of quotation marks and red zip ties on its products, and has initiated multiple lawsuits against companies, including Rastaclat, for unauthorized use. The brand's attempt to secure federal registration for the red zip tie has been preliminarily rejected by the USPTO due to concerns about similarity to existing trademarks, functionality, and lack of inherent distinctiveness. The article discusses the challenges Off-White faces in proving that these elements are source-identifying to consumers, rather than merely decorative.

title: Amazon to give Prime customers one-day shipping, cutting free delivery time in half
summary: Amazon.com Inc. plans to reduce its free delivery time for Prime subscribers from two days to one day. This change is expected to negatively impact profits in the second quarter as the company implements the new shipping model.

title: Chewy to fetch $1B in IPO
summary: Chewy.com, acquired by PetSmart, is preparing for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) that is expected to exceed $1 billion, significantly higher than initial estimates. The pet e-retailer will list under the ticker "CHWY" despite not yet being profitable, and PetSmart will retain control through Class B common stock. Analysts highlight Chewy's strong market share against Amazon and positive signs from its private label brands, despite the challenge of Amazon's expedited shipping.

title: HPE opens new headquarters in north San Jose
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise officially unveiled its new headquarters in north San Jose, bringing 1,300 workers to the America Center complex. San Jose Mayor Sam Liccardo lauded HPE's commitment to the community. The company also announced new corporate initiatives, including enhanced parental leave benefits and flexible work options, aiming to attract and retain top talent.
